Self-test simulation analysis

Source: R/9-self_test.R
self_test.Rd

Simulates data from an Rceattle model and refits the model to the simulated data, to check that the fitting procedure recovers the operating-model parameters. Pass process to redraw a process as well as the observations.

Usage

self_test(
  object = NULL,
  nsim = 50,
  simulate = TRUE,
  seed = 123,
  cores = NULL,
  getsd = NULL,
  phase = NULL,
  start = c("initial", "estimated"),
  debug = FALSE,
  timeout = Inf,
  process = FALSE,
  fit_control = NULL,
  Rceattle = NULL
)

Arguments

object

an Rceattle model fit using fit_mod().

nsim

number of simulations

simulate

passed to sim_mod. TRUE (default) simulates data with observation error; FALSE uses the model's expected values.

seed

random number seed. Simulation i uses seed + i, so results are reproducible under sequential and parallel execution alike.

cores

Number of cores for the parallel refits. Default NULL picks parallel::detectCores() - 6, capped at 2 under R CMD check (which sets _R_CHECK_LIMIT_CORES_). Set to 1 to force sequential execution.

getsd

whether each refit runs TMB::sdreport. Self-test compares refit point estimates to the operating model, so FALSE is faster with no effect on that comparison. NULL (default) inherits the input model's setting (TRUE only if it holds an sdrep).

phase

as in fit_mod. Under the default start = "initial" each refit covers the ground the original fit did, so a model that needed phasing for its real data needs it for every simulated one; without it such a model's refits can end many orders of magnitude from a zero gradient and be dropped as non-converged. NULL (default) reads what fit_mod() recorded on the source fit, so a model fitted under the package default phase = FALSE is refitted unphased.

start

Which parameter set each refit starts from: "initial" (default) or "estimated". See Details.

debug

return every simulation rather than only the converged ones. The dropped runs are the interesting ones when a self-test comes back short, and each holds its own $convergence diagnostics. See Value.

timeout

elapsed-second limit per simulation, Inf (default) for none. The optimizer runs with no iteration cap, so a replicate that wanders somewhere pathological can stall the run – a hang no convergence check can catch, because the fit never returns. One that exceeds the limit is stopped, counted as non-converged and reported separately. It is approximate: the limit is checked when control returns to R, so it fires between the optimizer's function evaluations rather than inside one.

process

passed to sim_mod. FALSE (default) keeps the fitted process deviations, so the test measures whether the estimator recovers its own parameters from new observations. Naming a process ("recruitment", "M", "growth", "dynamics", TRUE) redraws it, so the test instead measures recovery of a process the estimator has not been shown.

fit_control

optional fit_control() bundle for the refits. Only phase and getsd are read; see What fit_control() reaches.

Rceattle

deprecated name for object, still accepted so existing scripts keep working. Supplying both is an error.

Value

A list of Rceattle models named Sim_1, Sim_2, ... By default only the converged simulations, renumbered contiguously, with a message reporting how many were dropped. The list has class "Rceattle_selftest" and carries the number attempted in attr(, "nsim"), so printing it reports the convergence rate; it is otherwise the plain list it always was.

With debug = TRUE, every simulation, Sim_i being simulation i so it pairs with seed seed + i, plus the convergence verdicts in attr(, "converged"). A refit that errored outright comes back as the condition object rather than a model, so it cannot abort the run.

Where process redrew something, attr(, "process_sim") holds the deviations that generated each replicate, keyed by the same Sim_i names and subset alongside the models. Each entry names whichever of rec_dev, init_dev, log_M1_dev and beta_linkage_re were drawn, each with a same-shaped _drawn logical marking the cells the draw touched. Restrict any recovery statistic to those cells, and compare estimates against these rather than against the operating model, whose fitted deviations are no longer what generated the data.

Details

What start costs. "initial" uses initial_params, so the estimator travels the same distance to the optimum on simulated data as it did on the real data. "estimated" starts from the generating values instead – the fixed effects, and under random_rec = TRUE the inner Laplace problem too – so it is much faster and far likelier to converge, but on a multimodal or weakly identified surface the optimizer never leaves the basin containing them, so recovery is close to guaranteed by construction. Read it as optimistic about recovery, not merely less powerful. It is not a complete warm start either – fit_mod() resets log_Ftarget, proj_F_prop and the stock-recruit \(\alpha\)/\(\beta\) under both settings – and non-identifiability stays visible either way through $convergence's Hessian conditioning and estimability checks. What a warm start stops testing is reachability.

Interpreting the spread

sim_mod redraws the observations only, and warns about each row it leaves alone: a predator with empirical rather than estimated suitability has no predicted diet to draw from, and a covariance (MVN/MVNORM) survey fleet has no covariance outside its fitted years. Those data are identical in every replicate, so recovery of whatever they inform is optimistic.

By default recruitment is not redrawn, so under random_rec = TRUE every replicate shares the operating model's single realization – its shrunk empirical-Bayes modes, not a draw from N(0, sigmaR). The spread across replicates is then observation error alone and a lower bound on estimation uncertainty in SSB and recruitment, so do not read it against the model's own uncertainty bands, which include process error; and sigmaR is re-estimated from deviations shrunk toward zero the same way every time, a downward bias averaging does not remove. process = "recruitment" removes both, at the cost of asking a different question. See vignette("model-diagnostics").

Examples

# \donttest{
data(BS2017SS)
ss_run <- fit_mod(data_list = BS2017SS,
    inits = NULL, file = NULL,
    estimateMode = 0, random_rec = FALSE,
    msmMode = 0, avgnMode = 0,
    phase = FALSE, verbose = 0)
#> Warning: Passing ‘phase’, ‘verbose’ directly to fit_mod() is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Bundle these into fit_control() instead, e.g. fit_control(phase = ..., verbose = ...). Forwarding for now.
#> `age_trans_matrix` data does not span range of age for species 1 will fill with 0s
sims <- self_test(ss_run, nsim = 10)
# }
